biography: Gabriel Casagrande's journey began amidst the sun-drenched karting tracks of Paraná, Brazil. From the age of 10, he displayed a raw, untamed talent, quickly graduating from local races to national karting championships, often leaving older, more experienced drivers in his wake. A defining moment came at the 2012 Brazilian Karting Championship where, after starting last due to a mechanical issue, he carved his way through the field, securing a podium finish that caught the eye of AMM Motorsport. His transition to touring cars was swift, marked by aggressive overtaking and a relentless pursuit of victory. He spent time with Vogel Motorsport and A.Mattheis Vogel, honing his skills, but also clashing with team strategies he felt were too conservative. Now, at 27, and back with AMM Vogel, Casagrande is considered one of Brazil's most promising rising stars, hungry to prove his mettle on the international stage.
drivingStyle: Casagrande's driving style is characterized by a ferocious attack on corners and an unwavering commitment to late braking. He thrives under pressure, often pushing his car and tires to the absolute limit. His tire management can be inconsistent, a trade-off for his aggressive corner entry speeds. He favors a loose car setup, allowing him to rotate the car quickly, but requiring constant corrections and precise throttle control. He's known for his daring overtakes, often exploiting the smallest gaps, much to the chagrin of his competitors.
rivalries: Ricardo Silva: A long-standing rivalry stemming from their karting days. Silva, known for his calculated approach, often criticizes Casagrande's aggressive style, fueling their on-track battles.

Isabela Flores: A fierce competitor known for her consistency and tactical brilliance. Casagrande's attempts to intimidate her on track have been met with unwavering resolve, creating a tense atmosphere whenever they share the track.

Enzo Bellini: A young Italian driver who joined the series recently, Bellini has been very vocal with the media about Casagrande's driving. On track, this has led to a few incidents and retaliatory moves by both drivers.
quirks: Always wears the same pair of lucky socks he's had since his karting days, regardless of the weather.
Listens to a specific Brazilian samba song right before getting into the car to calm his nerves.
Refuses to look at the starting grid before the race, preferring to visualize his own strategy.
famousQuote: Second place is just the first loser.
careerHighlight: Winning the 2022 Stock Car Pro Series race at Interlagos. After a daring late-race pass on veteran driver Cacá Bueno, he held on to secure his first major victory, silencing his critics and proving his championship potential.
careerLowPoint: Crashing out of the lead on the final lap of the 2021 Cascavel race. A momentary lapse in concentration led to a costly mistake, costing him a certain victory and a significant blow to his championship hopes.
